To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

coexpression of the accessory subunit, Stac3, with human CaV1 (plus α2-δ1b and beta1a subunits), in the Xenopus oocyte expression system, increases plasma membrane expression and that this is a new platform that can be used for studying the voltage dependent properties of CaV channels without the complexity of skeletal muscle.

coexpression of the Stac3 protein dramatically increases the surface expression of CaV channels and that this is a useful new approach to investigate the voltage-dependent properties and disease-associated mutations in CaV channels.

coexpression of human Stac3 with human CaV1 (plus α2-δ1b and b1a subunits), in the absence of other accessory proteins, results in high expression of the Ca2+ channel complex at the plasma membrane and in functional currents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and cellular mechanisms of skeletal muscle excitability and the role of voltage-gated ion channels in the etiology of muscle disease.
the role of voltage-gated calcium channels in the etiology of human skeletal muscle disorders and the development of new tools to facilitate functional studies of these channels.
the voltage-dependent properties and gating of CaV1 and other ion channels, with a particular interest in how mutations of CaV1 cause human disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Stac3-enhances expression of CaV channels in Xenopus oocyte and reveals gating pore channels in HypoPP CaV1. 1 mutants.
Stac3 enhances expression and gating properties of CaV 1.1 in a Xenopus oocytes expression system.
the Stac3-enhancing effect is a novel and important tool for functional studies of CaV1, which is a major Ca2+ channel involved in skeletal muscle contraction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Stac3 enhances expression in oocytes and reveals a new class of leaky HypoPP mutant CaV1.2 channels.

Stac3 enhances expression in Xenopus oocyte of the skeletal muscle CaV1.2 channel, which can be used to investigate disease-associated mutations in HypoPP and to study the gating properties of CaV channels.
we show that Stac3 is an important co-factor for CaV1.3 and CaV1.2, and that Stac3 can enhance the expression of human skeletal muscle CaV1.4 in oocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Stac3 can enhance the expression of CaV at the plasma membrane, which can be exploited for the study of HypoPP mutants.
the Stac3/CaV1.1 interaction is sufficient to increase the expression of CaV channels in Xenopus oocyte expression studies.
the Stac3-CaV1.1 system is a powerful tool for studying HypoPP mutations and for investigating the biophysical properties of CaV.1 in the absence of a transverse tubule system.
